Composition marker for comp_iv() formulas

Source: R/formula_interface.R
ilr.Rd

A marker, valid only inside a formula passed to comp_iv(), that stands for the whole composition: the pivot isometric log-ratio (ILR) coordinates ilr1, ..., ilr{D-1}. The formula parser expands it before the model is fitted, and calling ilr() directly is an error.

Usage

ilr()

Value

None; ilr() signals an error when called outside a formula.

Details

A comp_iv() formula is fitted as written once ilr() is expanded, by one of two rules that depend on where the marker sits. No composition term is refused; only ilr() with arguments is an error.

Inside the formula operators + - * : / ^ %in% | || and parentheses, ilr() is replaced by the sum (ilr1 + ... + ilr{D-1}), and R's formula algebra applies to it. outcome ~ ilr() * sex fits the composition, sex and every composition-by-sex interaction; (ilr() | school) is an lme4 random slope on every coordinate. ilr()^2 means what (ilr1 + ilr2 + ilr3)^2 means in R: the main effects and every pairwise product of coordinates, with no squares.

Inside any other call, ilr() is distributed: the call is repeated once per coordinate and the copies are added. I(ilr()^2) becomes (I(ilr1^2) + ... + I(ilr{D-1}^2)) and poly(ilr(), 2) becomes (poly(ilr1, 2) + ... + poly(ilr{D-1}, 2)); splines::ns(), log() and scale() are treated alike. Every ilr() within one such call takes the same coordinate, so I(ilr() * ilr()) gives the squares; the pairwise products come from ilr()^2.

The full quadratic ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2) (main effects, squares and pairwise products) is the same model in every ILR basis, so its fit and its reallocations do not depend on the order of the parts. The fit of a squares-only or poly(ilr(), 2) specification depends on the part order given to declare_composition(). On the timeuse data, the odds ratio of obesity for 10 minutes moved from SB to MVPA under ilr() + I(ilr()^2) ranged from 0.828 to 0.834 across three part orders. comp_iv() fits the full quadratic without a formula through curvature = TRUE.

comp_iv() warns when the formula leaves out the composition's main effect, that is, when a coordinate appears neither as a term of its own nor as the first argument of poly(), ns() or bs().

See also

comp_iv(), whose formula argument accepts this marker.

Examples

cd <- declare_composition(timeuse, c("MVPA", "LPA", "SB", "SPT"),
                          closure = 1440)
# The composition enters via ilr(); sex and its interaction are
# ordinary terms
comp_iv(cd, obesity ~ ilr() * sex, model = "glm", family = "binomial")
#> <timecoda_fit> compositional generalized linear model (binomial)
#>   Parts: MVPA, LPA, SB, SPT (total = 1440)
#>   Reference composition: MVPA = 28.1, LPA = 235.5, SB = 677.2, SPT = 499.2
#> 
#> 
#> Call:  stats::glm(formula = obesity ~ (ilr1 + ilr2 + ilr3) * sex, family = "binomial", 
#>     data = data)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>  (Intercept)          ilr1          ilr2          ilr3       sexmale  
#>     -3.68401      -0.69592      -0.87505       1.52183       1.15199  
#> ilr1:sexmale  ilr2:sexmale  ilr3:sexmale  
#>      0.02295       1.14463      -1.06266  
#> 
#> Degrees of Freedom: 299 Total (i.e. Null);  292 Residual
#> Null Deviance:	    355.8 
#> Residual Deviance: 318.8 	AIC: 334.8
# A full quadratic in the composition, which does not depend on the
# part order
comp_iv(cd, zbmi ~ ilr()^2 + I(ilr()^2) + sex, model = "lm")
#> <timecoda_fit> compositional linear model
#>   Parts: MVPA, LPA, SB, SPT (total = 1440)
#>   Reference composition: MVPA = 28.1, LPA = 235.5, SB = 677.2, SPT = 499.2
#> 
#> 
#> Call:
#> stats::lm(formula = zbmi ~ (ilr1 + ilr2 + ilr3)^2 + (I(ilr1^2) + 
#>     I(ilr2^2) + I(ilr3^2)) + sex, data = data)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)         ilr1         ilr2         ilr3    I(ilr1^2)    I(ilr2^2)  
#>    -2.42867     -0.98660      0.04431      1.59720     -0.04117      0.53721  
#>   I(ilr3^2)      sexmale    ilr1:ilr2    ilr1:ilr3    ilr2:ilr3  
#>    -1.06062     -0.07917     -0.15457     -0.22287      0.18520  
#>
